parsed.explanation: The operative regime criminalises same-sex conduct up to life imprisonment (mainland) and five years (semi-autonomous jurisdiction), and — critically for a trans visitor — the record documents that law being used as a police lever: a state-declared 'witch hunt', forced anal examinations, a regional committee hunting 'homosexuals' online, custody torture, and deportation of service staff. That is tier-2 state-tolerated/directed targeting with severe consequences, plus a 2024 mutilation attack on a trans activist and government blocking of LGBTIQ information. Uncertainty (whether statutes remain in force as written, thin post-2024 data) does not soften an enforced pattern; the last documented enforcement wave is recent and the hostility trajectory is escalating, not reforming.

entry_documents.exposure: No document-specific border practices documented; 'unknown', but any immigration encounter with mismatched presentation risks referral into the criminalisation apparatus.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry scrutiny can cascade into investigation and detention under 'gross indecency' or identity-punishment campaigns.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented torture and rape of gay men in police custody (2013 report); forced anal examinations in 2018 witch hunt; 17-member police-lawyer-doctor committee to identify and punish homosexuals.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented; lack of access to justice listed as a top national problem.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Criminal statutes provide the charging basis; custody abuse documented as practice, not anomaly.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility/custody-placement rules specific to trans visitors documented.

care_services.exposure: Deportation of HIV/AIDS staff (2017) disrupted services; documented climate of discrimination limits rights enjoyment.
care_services.protection: Nursing/midwifery and family-planning rules bar sexual-orientation discrimination in care (2010/2013/2017); enforcement not established.
care_services.interaction: Paper protections coexist with documented service disruption; operating value unknown.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State framing of LGBT people as punishable: officials declared a witch hunt, constituted a punishment committee, deported rights workers, block LGBTIQ websites; 'weaponisation of law' documented 2024.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Broadcast/online hate-speech codes exist but enforcement unresolved and 2020 online regs repealed prior bans.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official hostility raises both outing probability and severity of every other axis.

minors_guardians.exposure: Semi-autonomous penal decree sets under-18 sexual-offence thresholds; no youth-specific care provision beyond counselling language; criminalisation exposes a travelling minor's companion if outed together.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult-with-minor travel inherits the same criminalisation and custody exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2024 abduction and mutilation of trans activist (ears cut, found beaten in forest); activists document substantial prejudice, discrimination and violence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: UN condemnation and constitutional equality guarantees exist; no documented prosecution of attackers or working recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are documented as perpetrators, not protectors; reporting risk appears to exceed remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Access to justice is a top-three national problem; whether statutes remain in force as written unresolved; no post-2024 statistics.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Media-council hate-speech code; healthcare non-discrimination texts — operating status unverified.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin post-2024 record is not evidence of improvement in a state with documented, recent enforcement.

anchor_checks.comparison: Comparable in severity — morality-policing sweeps, coerced examination, torture in custody, life-scale penalties — but 0.15-C documents continuous decoy-driven sweeps against presentation itself; here the 2018 campaign is city-scoped and dated, and no cross-dressing statute is documented, so this sits slightly above that anchor.

Similar: criminal statutes plus birth-document/criminal exposure and weak recourse. This jurisdiction adds documented state witch hunts, forced anal exams and custody torture, making it materially worse than the 0.25 anchor's brief-sentences tier.

Above that anchor: 0.35-B involves hours-long checks and release without imprisonment; here documented outcomes include torture, deportation and mutilation-level violence with impunity, so the severity is a tier higher.

Very close: border detention, custody abuse, and unenforced-formal remedies mirror that anchor; this dossier lacks documented border-specific targeting of trans visitors, which is the residual mitigation keeping it at the top of the 0.15–0.25 band rather than below.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime pairs maximum-severity criminal statutes (life imprisonment) with documented state enforcement campaigns against LGBT people — anal examinations, internet hunts, custody torture, and staff deportation — meaning the sexuality law is not a dead letter but an operating police lever that a visibly trans visitor is well placed to trigger. Compounding this, government blocking of LGBTIQ information and a documented climate of escalating hostility (per the 2024 'We Are Facing Extinction' report) raise outing probability and remove support infrastructure. The only counterweights are paper healthcare non-discrimination and constitutional equality language, none documented as operating. The most recent incident is 2024 and no post-2024 relief is documented. Structural signals — criminalisation, no recognition, poor access to justice, state hostility — resolve the thin-data gaps toward the risk they imply: high-severity, state-tolerated targeting with negligible recourse.
